DATA PATH

Website → HarborWise API → trained models

The API (FastAPI) runs in a container on IBM LinuxONE (s390x). The same container trains the models. Status: checking…

Routes: POST /recommendations, GET /experiments, GET /data-quality, GET /health.

DATASET

Caribbean port calls, 2019

Iphar et al., Data in Brief (2024), Zenodo 10380638 v1.1.0, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0. 1,488,781 AIS port calls → 51,729 commercial berth visits (6,218 ships, 832 berths, 159 ports). 82.67% of calls match a surveyed berth polygon.

Dataset on Zenodo
MODELS

Three models, one window

Tuned XGBoost predicts the hours left alongside (test MAE 14.55 h vs 16.56 h for the berth median). A random forest with class weights and isotonic calibration predicts "clears within 6 h" (PR-AUC 0.66). An XGBoost quantile model with a conformal shift gives P25/P50/P90 (coverage 23.7 / 48.8 / 89.6%). Split by time: train Jan–Aug, validation Sep–Oct, test Nov–Dec 2019.

DECISION

Lowest total cost inside the risk limit

J(v) = fuel cost + λ·(sailing + expected wait) + μ·(expected idle berth). Fuel follows the cubic speed law (Psaraftis & Kontovas 2013); CO₂ = 3.114 t per t fuel (IMO MEPC.308(73)). λ is set so service speed is optimal when there is no queue; μ = $500/h. Late risk = chance the berth is free for longer than the allowed flexibility before the ship arrives.

WHAT IS ILLUSTRATIVE

Simulated, and labelled

The five ships and their routes are demo voyages. Port queue panels and the replay map are illustrative. Fuel and CO₂ use illustrative engine figures. Anchorage waits cannot be observed in this dataset; the E11 replay derives them.

OPEN SOURCE

Built with

XGBoost, scikit-learn, imbalanced-learn, pandas, FastAPI, React, Leaflet, Natural Earth. Coastline: Natural Earth 1:110m (public domain).
